deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the station-by-station register from the previous folio: Gauss's reduction of the Hanoverian triangulation (the Bremen–Stade–Hamburg area, measured in the 1820s) onto his conformal plane coordinates. The left margin is cut off in the image, so the first letters of the target names are lost.

General format. Each block has a station name as heading ('X act.' = observing station X). Under it, each line is a target station, a direction (azimuth) in degrees.minutes.seconds,thousandths, and sometimes a small correction in arcseconds. On the previous page some stations also have their plane coordinates (x, y) in metres. The azimuths are in Gauss's convention, i.e. bearings in the plane of his conformal projection.

What the correction is (inferred). The correction is the reduction of the observed spheroidal direction to the chord in the plane: the angle between the image of the geodesic and the straight chord, in modern terms the arc-to-chord ('t–T') correction. Its size is roughly Δx(2y1+y2)ρ/(6R²).

Test of this reading (my own check on the previous page's data):
- Sandstedt→Neuenkirchen: 183°57'49.758" + 3.346" = 183°57'53.104".
- Neuenkirchen→Sandstedt: 3°57'56.435" − 3.331" = 3°57'53.104".
- The two corrected bearings differ by exactly 180°.
So the corrected value is the plane bearing of the chord. Reciprocal corrections are of opposite sign and nearly equal magnitude here.

This page, block by block:
(1) Asendorf act. (Asendorf near Twistringen, Diepholz district). Directions:
- [?]ikberg 25°49'41.503"
- Twistringen 98°14'4.841", with correction +0.646"
- [?]kenberg (probably Falkenberg) 262°12'9.956"
- [?]ttonberg (or similar) 312°41'20.645"
(2) Twistringen. Directions:
- [Br]emen 20°32'37.700" +6.259", corrected chord bearing 20°32'43.959"
- [Ase]ndorf 98°14'4.841" +0.646"
(3) Ahlerstedt. Directions:
- [Wi]lsede 129°39'26.245"
- [Lit]berg 102°10'47.649"
(4) Elsdorf. Directions:
- [Ha]mburg, with no value entered
- [Lit]berg 250°36'53.043"
(5) Hollenstedt. Directions:
- [Lit]berg 288°7'32.546"
- [?]stedt 183°28'16", unfinished and overwritten

The Asendorf/Twistringen blocks, and the upper part of what follows, are cancelled by a large red X.

There is no derivation as such on the page. It is tabulation in service of the coordinate computation of secondary (church-tower) points, done by forward intersection from bearings to known stations. Examples are Apensen, Buxtehude and Stade on the previous page, which were fixed from Hamburg/Litberg/Wilsede bearings.
errors: Under Twistringen, the bearing to Asendorf is written 98°14'4.841" +0.646". This is identical to the Asendorf→Twistringen entry. By the convention verified on the previous page, the reciprocal bearing should be about 278°14'5.487" minus a correction of opposite sign (≈ −0.65"). The line looks like a mechanical copy, which plausibly explains the red cancellation of the block.
The Hollenstedt→[?]stedt value 183.28.16 is incomplete (no decimals) and overwritten. The Elsdorf→Hamburg line has no value. The page is unfinished.

results.what: Register of plane (conformal-projection) bearings, with arc-to-chord reductions, for secondary stations Asendorf, Twistringen, Ahlerstedt, Elsdorf, Hollenstedt in the Hanoverian survey
results.modern_name: Grid bearings with t–T (arc-to-chord) correction in Gauss conformal (Gauss–Krüger-type) coordinates
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Hanoverian survey 1821–1830s; later systematized by Schreiber and Krüger)

deep.surprise_reason: Pure survey bookkeeping from Gauss's well-documented Hanoverian triangulation. There is no new mathematics, and the method (conformal plane coordinates with direction reductions) is well known to be his.

transcription_corrections: The truncated names are likely: '[?]kenberg' = Falkenberg; '[?]emen' = Bremen; '[?]ndorf' = Asendorf; '[?]lsede' = Wilsede; '[?]lberg' = Litberg (Ahlerstedt, Elsdorf and Hollenstedt blocks); '[?]mburg' = Hamburg. '[?]ikberg' and '[?]ttonberg' remain uncertain.
Under Twistringen the image reads '98.14.4.841' (with a point, not a comma, before 841), as in the transcription.
Hollenstedt's last line reads '183.28.16.' with the digits overwritten, not cleanly struck through. A large red pencil X cancels the Asendorf/Twistringen blocks.
